name: zai-coding-endpoint
purpose: ZAI's `zai_endpoint` switch: chat-completions.js:2552 chooses between API_ZAI_CODING and API_ZAI_COMMON with a single ternary, and until this scenario all four zai captures omitted the field, so the rule existed only as a source-derived unit test. The scenario sends zai_endpoint 'coding' and records the resulting URL, whose PATH carries the mode (/api/coding/paas/v4 rather than /api/paas/v4) because the redirect below rewrites only the ORIGIN: a capture that showed the common path would be the switch failing, not a normalisation.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port, so the authority is not stable

tier2.rule: value replaced with Bearer <redacted>, presence and scheme preserved
tier2.reason: The scenario supplies a synthetic key; the credential itself is asserted by expectedAuthorizationKey.

tier2.rule: the recorder ORIGIN is replaced with <mock>; the path stays
tier2.reason: Only the ephemeral authority is rewritten, so the recorded target still contains /api/coding/paas/v4 and therefore shows WHICH literal the ternary chose. Rewriting the whole base instead would make the two modes produce identical bytes, and the scenario would assert nothing about zai_endpoint.
tier2.pinnedSource: src/endpoints/backends/chat-completions.js:2552 defaultApiUrl = request.body.zai_endpoint === ZAI_ENDPOINT.CODING ? API_ZAI_CODING : API_ZAI_COMMON; :95 API_ZAI_CODING = 'https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
